evidence: src/application/AdvanceOrderUseCase.ts, CancelOrderUseCase.ts and GetOrderUseCase.ts all call loadOrder(this.orders, orderId) from src/application/OrderLoader.ts, so the not-found rule lives in one place.

AdvanceOrderUseCase.ts, CancelOrderUseCase.ts, GetOrderUseCase.ts, ListOrdersUseCase.ts and PlaceOrderUseCase.ts all return toOrderDto(...) from src/application/OrderDtoMapper.ts, so Order→OrderDto mapping is done in one place.

Each stock side effect appears once: this.stock.reserve in PlaceOrderUseCase.ts, this.stock.dispatch (when target === 'shipped') in AdvanceOrderUseCase.ts, and this.stock.release in CancelOrderUseCase.ts.
src/application/ListStockLevelsUseCase.ts builds StockLevelDto only here and uses the domain's p.available instead of recomputing it.
src/application/dtos.ts holds all input and output contracts (PlaceOrderInput, OrderDto, OrderLineDto, StockLevelDto) used across the module.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module is a cohesive application layer: use cases that coordinate domain objects and return DTOs for order fulfilment and stock levels. The module's own helpers are used consistently:
- Every use case that turns an order into a DTO calls toOrderDto from OrderDtoMapper.ts.
- Every use case that looks up an order by id calls loadOrder from OrderLoader.ts.
- PlaceOrderUseCase creates a new order and ListOrdersUseCase reads lists, so neither needs loadOrder.

Each stock side effect is written in only one place:
- reserve when an order is placed (PlaceOrderUseCase)
- dispatch when an order is shipped (AdvanceOrderUseCase)
- release when an order is cancelled (CancelOrderUseCase)

ListStockLevelsUseCase builds its StockLevelDto inline. The module has no stock mapper, and this is the only place that DTO is built, so nothing is bypassed or duplicated. It also takes the available amount from the domain's p.available instead of working it out again. OrderLineInput and OrderLineDto have the same shape, but one is input and the other is output, and neither holds a rule. No violations found.
